agenda: Reports of the Secretary-General on the Sudan and South Sudan; Report of the Secretary-General on the situation in Abyei (S/2025/649)
members: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

steps.intent: As penholder, our primary objective is to secure a 12-month extension of UNISFA's mandate and JBVMM support while maintaining pressure on South Sudan to withdraw the SSPDF from southern Abyei and on Sudan to issue pending visas for UN police. We anticipate pushback from the Russian Federation and China regarding Chapter VII references, critical language on Sudanese visa delays, and references to climate-related security impacts, as well as sensitivity from the A3+1 (Algeria, Sierra Leone, Somalia, Guyana) regarding sovereignty concerns of both Juba and Khartoum. However, by adhering closely to agreed language from resolution 2760 (2024) while strictly updating necessary dates and factual context regarding the Sudan crisis, we expect to preserve consensus or secure at least 13-14 affirmative votes without triggering a veto.

United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort.change: Condemning the ongoing conflict in Sudan, including grave violations of international humanitarian law and violations and abuses of human rights, particularly conflict-related sexual violence and violations against children, further expressing grave concern over the adverse impacts of the conflict on the Abyei Area, including the influx of displaced persons, the obstruction of engagement between Sudan and South Sudan to resolve the area’s political status, and the disruption of the JBVMM’s aerial monitoring operations due to ongoing hostilities and airspace restrictions,

Calls upon the authorities in Sudan and South Sudan, as well as local leaders, to support UNISFA’s community-level conflict prevention and mediation efforts, to promote peaceful seasonal transhumance, and to de-escalate tensions, including between the Ngok Dinka and Twic Dinka communities, and encourages the full, equal, meaningful and safe participation of women and youth in all peacebuilding and conflict mitigation mechanisms;

messages.Algeria: Algeria fully supports the renewal of UNISFA's mandate and its crucial role in maintaining stability and protecting civilians in the Abyei Area. However, the draft must maintain a balanced approach that respects Sudan's sovereignty and takes into account the extraordinary challenges currently confronting the Sudanese authorities. We urge the penholder to adopt more constructive phrasing regarding visa issuance and administrative coordination between Sudan and UNISFA.
messages.China: China supports the renewal of UNISFA's mandate and appreciates the mission's positive contribution to stabilizing Abyei and the border area. The Security Council should fully respect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Sudan and South Sudan, heed their legitimate concerns, and avoid exerting excessive unilateral pressure or naming and shaming host authorities who are operating under exceptionally challenging domestic circumstances. We look forward to working constructively with the penholder and Council colleagues to reach consensus on the draft text.
messages.Denmark: Denmark thanks the United States for circulating this draft and fully supports the timely renewal of UNISFA's mandate, which remains indispensable for stability and civilian protection in Abyei. Given the catastrophic human rights situation across the Sudan, we ask to explicitly reflect the scourge of conflict-related sexual violence and ensure the WPS language consistently includes the 'safe' participation of women. We look forward to engaging constructively towards a smooth adoption.
messages.France: France strongly supports the draft resolution and commends the United States for preparing a balanced text that ensures the continuity of UNISFA's vital mission amidst alarming regional instability. In light of the grave human rights and humanitarian situation spilling over from the conflict in Sudan, we propose modest additions to underline accountability and ensure consistency with Council standards regarding the safe participation of women. We look forward to voting in favour of this text.
messages.Greece: Greece strongly supports the draft resolution and thanks the United States for circulating a well-balanced text that ensures the uninterrupted mandate of UNISFA and vital support to the JBVMM. We welcome the draft's clear emphasis on the demilitarization of Abyei, the safety and security of peacekeepers, unhindered humanitarian access, and accountability. We propose a minor addition in operative paragraph 7 to align the reference to women's participation with agreed Women, Peace, and Security language, and we stand ready to vote in favour of the resolution.
messages.Guyana: Guyana commends the United States for preparing this draft and strongly supports the one-year extension of UNISFA's mandate and its crucial support to the JBVMM. In line with the shared perspective of the A3+, we believe the text should adequately reflect the vital role played by regional mechanisms, specifically the African Union and IGAD, in mediating between the parties and facilitating progress on Abyei's status. We also welcome the text's attention to civilian protection, humanitarian access, and the compounding effects of climate-induced shocks on local stability.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan fully supports the renewal of UNISFA's mandate and commends the dedication and sacrifice of peacekeepers operating under increasingly challenging circumstances. To foster greater cooperation between the mission and the host authorities, we propose more constructive language regarding visa processing and administrative procedures. We reaffirm our steadfast commitment to the sovereignty, unity, and territorial integrity of both Sudan and South Sudan.
messages.Panama: Panama commends the United States for its leadership as penholder and fully supports the renewal of UNISFA's mandate at this critical juncture for Sudan and South Sudan. We appreciate the draft's strong emphasis on the protection of civilians, humanitarian access, and international humanitarian law. To ensure consistency with recent Council language and our shared commitments under the Women, Peace and Security agenda, we suggest adding 'and safe' regarding women's participation in OP7.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea strongly supports the draft resolution renewing UNISFA's mandate and JBVMM support for another year, as well as the penholder's efforts to address the compounding security and humanitarian challenges facing the Abyei Area. We particularly welcome the robust language on civilian protection, unhindered humanitarian access, and the urgent necessity for Sudan to remove bureaucratic obstacles, including visa delays for UN police. Our modest textual suggestions aim to reinforce consistency on Women, Peace, and Security language and underscore accountability for attacks against peacekeepers in line with resolution 2589 (2021).
messages.Russian Federation: The draft must reflect a balanced and objective approach that respects the sovereignty of Sudan and avoids disproportionate finger-pointing against Khartoum, which is operating under extraordinarily difficult conditions to preserve statehood. We must also refrain from burdening the mandate of UNISFA with unjustified and controversial thematic concepts such as climate-related security narratives. The Council should focus on constructive engagement with the host authorities to resolve practical administrative questions rather than resorting to pressure and public reproach.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone, acting in solidarity with the A3+, welcomes the draft resolution renewing the mandate of UNISFA and its support for the JBVMM, which remain indispensable for peace and stability along the border. We emphasize the vital importance of anchoring political progress in African-led mediation frameworks, particularly the African Union and IGAD. We urge the penholder to adopt constructive, balanced language that fosters cooperation between Juba, Khartoum, and UNISFA, while recognizing the profound humanitarian and displacement pressures confronting the Abyei Area.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia fully supports the renewal of UNISFA's mandate and appreciates the United States' leadership on this text, particularly regarding civilian protection, humanitarian access, and climate-related security impacts. To reflect Council consensus and established Women, Peace, and Security standards, we request the explicit inclusion of 'safe' participation of women in OP7 and a reference to addressing conflict-related sexual violence. We look forward to supporting this draft resolution's swift adoption.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the renewal of UNISFA's mandate for an additional year and commends the United States for circulating this balanced draft. As a member of the region, we emphasize the indispensable role of IGAD alongside the African Union in facilitating dialogue between Sudan and South Sudan on the status of Abyei. We also encourage a collaborative and constructive approach between the United Nations and the Sudanese authorities on administrative matters, particularly in light of the severe conflict and complex operational circumstances facing Sudan.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom strongly supports the draft resolution renewing UNISFA's mandate and thanks the United States for its leadership as penholder. Given the dire security and humanitarian reality across the region, it is essential that the Council clearly condemns conflict-related sexual violence, which remains widespread and devastating. We also encourage standardizing our agreed Women, Peace, and Security language in OP7 to reflect women's full, equal, meaningful, and safe participation.

steps.summary: As penholder, the United States revised the draft resolution to reflect broad Council consensus by incorporating agreed Women, Peace and Security language, explicit condemnations of conflict-related sexual violence, and recognition of regional mediation efforts by the African Union and IGAD. To accommodate concerns from the A3+, China, Pakistan, and the Russian Federation without compromising the mission's operational requirements, balanced compromise language based on resolution 2760 (2024) was introduced regarding visa processing and administrative cooperation with host authorities, while firmly preserving the mandate's Chapter VII authority and demilitarization requirements.

messages.Algeria: Algeria thanks the United States for its constructive engagement and for incorporating our views into Revision 1, particularly regarding the balanced language on cooperation between the Sudanese authorities and UNISFA, as well as the unequivocal call for the demilitarization of the Abyei Area. The current text strikes a sound balance and provides UNISFA with the necessary backing to continue its critical stabilization and peacekeeping mission. Algeria is prepared to vote in favour of the draft resolution as formulated.
messages.China: China thanks the penholder for constructive engagements and for accommodating our concerns by incorporating agreed language on visa facilitation and climate impacts. We support the draft resolution to extend the mandate of UNISFA and JBVMM, which play an important role in maintaining stability in the Abyei Area. China stands ready to vote in favour of the text as currently drafted.
messages.Denmark: Denmark thanks the United States for incorporating our key priorities into Revision 1, particularly on the safe, full, equal, and meaningful participation of women, the condemnation of conflict-related sexual violence, and the protection of humanitarian personnel. The draft effectively equips UNISFA and the JBVMM to navigate a highly volatile environment while reinforcing vital humanitarian and human rights standards. Denmark fully supports the text as currently drafted and stands ready to vote in favour.
messages.France: France thanks the United States for incorporating our proposals regarding accountability and the safe participation of women into revision 1. The draft presents a balanced and necessary renewal of UNISFA's mandate in a critical regional context, fully reflecting our priorities on the protection of civilians, international humanitarian law, and the safety of peacekeepers. France fully supports the adoption of the resolution as drafted.
messages.Greece: Greece thanks the United States for accommodating our proposal on the full, equal, meaningful and safe participation of women in the revised draft. The current text strikes a balanced and constructive approach, robustly supporting UNISFA's mandate, the safety of peacekeepers, international humanitarian law, and the stabilization of Abyei. Greece fully supports the draft resolution and looks forward to voting in favour.
messages.Guyana: Guyana expresses its appreciation to the United States as penholder for constructively engaging with our delegation and incorporating our proposals regarding the role of IGAD and regional mediation frameworks. The revised text provides a balanced, comprehensive basis to ensure UNISFA's continued mandate implementation, protection of civilians, and support for stability in Abyei. Guyana is pleased to support the draft resolution as currently formulated and looks forward to its unanimous adoption.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan thanks the United States for its constructive engagement and for accommodating our suggestions regarding cooperative dialogue with the host authorities on operational matters. We support the draft resolution to extend UNISFA's mandate, recognizing the mission's vital contribution to regional stability, civilian protection, and border monitoring. Pakistan reaffirms its unwavering commitment to the sovereignty, unity, and territorial integrity of both Sudan and South Sudan.
messages.Panama: Panama thanks the United States for accommodating our proposal regarding the full, equal, meaningful and safe participation of women in paragraph 7. We fully support the draft resolution as currently drafted, which provides vital continuity for UNISFA while reinforcing the protection of civilians, humanitarian access, and international humanitarian law. Panama looks forward to voting in favour of this balanced text.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea thanks the United States for incorporating our proposals regarding the safety and security of peacekeepers under resolution 2589 (2021) and the full, equal, meaningful and safe participation of women. We find the current draft well-balanced, addressing the critical operational and protection needs of UNISFA while urging constructive dialogue between Sudan and South Sudan. The Republic of Korea fully supports the text as revised and looks forward to voting in favour of its adoption.
messages.Russian Federation: We take note of the penholder's efforts to adjust the language on visa issuance in PP11 and OP4, but we remain convinced that the Council must avoid an unbalanced approach that singles out Khartoum while it confronts an acute national crisis. Furthermore, we reiterate our principled objection to artificial linkages between climate change and security in Council mandates, which do not reflect consensus. Further accommodation on these points is necessary to secure our delegation's support on the draft.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone thanks the United States for incorporating our proposals regarding the central facilitation roles of the African Union and IGAD in OP6, as well as the recognition in PP6 of the heavy burden borne by host communities in Abyei. On OP5, we reiterate our call for constructive, standard Council language on the redeployment of South Sudanese personnel rather than rigid formulations that may hamper ongoing cooperation between Juba and UNISFA. With this adjustment, our delegation is ready to fully support the adoption of this resolution.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia thanks the United States for accommodating our proposals regarding conflict-related sexual violence and the full, equal, meaningful, and safe participation of women. The revised draft strikes an appropriate balance, reinforces UNISFA's vital mandate for civilian protection and border monitoring, and properly reflects international humanitarian law obligations. Slovenia is satisfied with the text and is ready to vote in favour.
messages.Somalia: Somalia thanks the penholder for incorporating our inputs into Revision 1, notably the inclusion of IGAD and a more constructive framing regarding visa issuance and engagement with the Government of Sudan. We believe this draft strikes a balanced and realistic approach that supports UNISFA's stabilizing mandate and regional peace efforts. Somalia is ready to vote in favour of the resolution as drafted.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom thanks the United States as penholder for constructively incorporating our proposals regarding conflict-related sexual violence, violations and abuses against children, and the full, equal, meaningful and safe participation of women. We fully support the current text renewing UNISFA's mandate and the JBVMM's support tasks, which are vital for regional stability amid the wider crisis in Sudan. The United Kingdom is ready to vote in favour of the resolution as drafted.

steps.summary: As penholder, the United States accommodated Sierra Leone's proposal on the redeployment of South Sudanese personnel in paragraph 5 to consolidate regional and A3 consensus. Requests from the Russian Federation to remove references to the adverse effects of climate change and dilute language on visa issuance were rejected to preserve critical Council standards on peacekeeper deployment and environmental drivers of instability. The draft resolution is poised for adoption with 14 votes in favour and one abstention.

reasons.China: China consistently supports the renewal of UNISFA's mandate to maintain stability in Abyei and along the border, and all key concerns regarding sovereignty and balanced language were adequately addressed in the text.
reasons.Denmark: Denmark fully supports the renewal of UNISFA's mandate and the JBVMM mechanism to maintain stability in Abyei, particularly given the conflict in Sudan, and will vote in favour of the US-drafted resolution.
reasons.France: France consistently supports the renewal of UNISFA's mandate to maintain stability in Abyei and along the border, and all of France's key priorities regarding international humanitarian law, accountability, and peacekeeper safety were incorporated into the final text.
reasons.Greece: Greece consistently supports the renewal of UNISFA's mandate and JBVMM support, in alignment with international law, peacekeeping safety, and WPS principles, and sees no need to make an explanation of vote prior to adoption.
reasons.Guyana: Guyana consistently supports the renewal of UNISFA's mandate to maintain stability, protect civilians, and support regional mediation efforts in Abyei, in alignment with our established voting record and our A3+ partners.
reasons.Pakistan: Pakistan supports the extension of UNISFA’s mandate as an essential stabilizing presence along the border between Sudan and South Sudan, consistent with our support throughout negotiations and our commitment to the sovereignty and territorial integrity of both countries.
reasons.Panama: Panama supports the renewal of UNISFA's mandate to maintain stability and protect civilians in Abyei, particularly appreciating the inclusion of language on women, peace, and security and international humanitarian law. In line with Council practice, Panama does not need to deliver an explanation of vote prior to voting in favour.
reasons.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea supports the renewal of UNISFA's mandate to maintain stability, protect civilians, and support border monitoring in Abyei, and our key priorities regarding peacekeeper safety (resolution 2589) and women's participation were accommodated.

reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom strongly supports the renewal of UNISFA's mandate and the JBVMM, which remain essential for stability in Abyei and along the border, and all of our key priorities, including strong language on conflict-related sexual violence and child protection, have been reflected in the final text.
reasons.United States of America: As the penholder and author of the draft resolution renewing the mandate of UNISFA and its support for the JBVMM for an additional year, the United States strongly supports its adoption and will vote in favour.

after.Russian Federation:
(spoke in Russian):

The Russian Federation abstained in the voting on the draft resolution submitted by the United States extending the mandate of the United Nations Interim Security Force for Abyei (UNISFA) and its support for the Joint Border Verification and Monitoring Mechanism.

At the outset, we wish to reaffirm our high appreciation for the work of UNISFA personnel, who continue to carry out their duties under exceptionally complex and dangerous conditions, playing an important stabilizing role in Abyei and along the border between Sudan and South Sudan.

At the same time, we cannot overlook the fact that the text presented to the Council once again suffers from a lack of balance and reflects the narrow approaches of the American penholder. Regrettably, our constructive comments and proposals, as well as the concerns voiced by the host countries, were largely disregarded during the work on the draft.

In particular, we find unacceptable the persistent attempts to place undue pressure and blame on the sovereign authorities of the Sudan and South Sudan, including with regard to visa issuance and administrative arrangements, while turning a blind eye to the profound and tragic realities currently facing the Sudan. The ongoing military confrontation against rebel forces in the country naturally complicates state administrative processes. Instead of demonstrating genuine understanding and fostering constructive engagement with Khartoum and Juba, the sponsors continue to rely on finger-pointing and pressure tactics.

Furthermore, we must once again object to the artificial encumbering of the mission’s mandate with controversial, non-consensus thematic concepts, including attempts to link security challenges to the climate agenda. Inserting such extraneous issues does not contribute to resolving the actual tasks of stabilization and civilian protection on the ground.

We remain convinced that any sustainable solution to the problem of Abyei can be achieved exclusively through direct, mutually respectful dialogue between Khartoum and Juba, on the basis of existing bilateral agreements and with full respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of both States, free from external dictate.

Russia will continue to support efforts aimed at normalizing relations between the Sudan and South Sudan and establishing lasting peace in the region.
after.Sierra Leone:
I have the honour to deliver this statement on behalf of the three African members of the Security Council, namely, Algeria, Somalia and my own country, Sierra Leone, as well as Guyana (A3+).

At the outset, the A3+ wishes to express our appreciation to the United States, the penholder, for its efforts in facilitating consultations and steering the negotiations leading to the adoption of the resolution renewing the mandate of the United Nations Interim Security Force for Abyei (UNISFA) and its support to the Joint Border Verification and Monitoring Mechanism (JBVMM). 

The A3+ voted in favour of this resolution because we firmly believe that UNISFA’s presence remains vital to maintaining peace, stability, and security in the Abyei Area and along the border between Sudan and South Sudan. For over a decade, UNISFA has served as a crucial buffer, deterring violence, protecting civilians, and facilitating intercommunal dialogue, while the JBVMM continues to play an indispensable role in promoting border security and cooperation.

We remain gravely concerned by the compounding security and humanitarian challenges facing the Abyei Area, which have been severely exacerbated by the catastrophic conflict in the Sudan. The intensified fighting and devastating violence in Sudan, including recent escalations, have triggered substantial waves of displacement into Abyei, placing immense strain on already scarce local resources and fragile infrastructure. This situation is further aggravated by the adverse impacts of climate change, particularly recurring severe floods that undermine livelihoods and exacerbate food insecurity.

In this context, the A3+ underlines the urgent need for enhanced international humanitarian support to assist the affected populations and host communities. We also reiterate our call for unhindered, safe, and rapid humanitarian access to all civilians in need.

The A3+ reaffirms its unwavering commitment to the sovereignty, unity, and territorial integrity of both Sudan and South Sudan. We reiterate that Abyei must remain a demilitarized and weapons-free zone. We urge both parties to honor their commitments under the 2011 Agreement, immediately withdraw all unauthorized military and armed personnel from the Abyei Area, and refrain from any unilateral actions that could jeopardize peace or alter the status of the territory.

While acknowledging the severe constraints imposed by the ongoing conflict in Sudan, we stress that a lasting solution to the final status of Abyei can only be achieved through peaceful dialogue and political negotiations between the two sisterly nations. We encourage the African Union, through the African Union High-Level Implementation Panel, alongside the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) and the United Nations Special Envoy for the Horn of Africa, to continue their mediation and facilitation efforts.

We also commend UNISFA’s ongoing community-level peacebuilding initiatives, including its support for traditional leaders, local peace committees, and intercommunal dialogue among the Ngok Dinka, the Misseriya, and the Twic Dinka communities. In this regard, we emphasize the imperative of ensuring the full, equal, and meaningful participation of women and youth in all peace and reconciliation processes.

Finally, the A3+ pays tribute to the leadership and personnel of UNISFA, as well as to the troop- and police-contributing countries, for their courage, steadfast dedication, and sacrifice in service of peace in Abyei under increasingly complex and perilous conditions.

I thank you.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
The United Kingdom welcomes the adoption of today’s resolution renewing the mandate of the United Nations Interim Security Force for Abyei (UNISFA) and its support to the Joint Border Verification and Monitoring Mechanism (JBVMM). We thank the United States, as penholder, for leading the negotiations, and Council members for their constructive engagement.

UNISFA continues to play an indispensable role in maintaining stability, protecting civilians, and facilitating intercommunal dialogue in Abyei. However, the mission operates in an increasingly volatile and precarious environment. The catastrophic conflict in Sudan continues to inflict immense suffering across the country and has severe repercussions for Abyei and the wider region, driving thousands of displaced people into the area and placing acute pressure on already scarce resources and local communities. 

Against this backdrop, the full implementation of UNISFA’s mandate is more critical than ever. We reiterate our call on the parties to uphold the demilitarized status of the Abyei Area. The presence of South Sudan People’s Defence Forces and other armed elements in Abyei is contrary to agreed frameworks and undermines stability; all unauthorized forces must be withdrawn without delay.

Furthermore, we urge both Sudan and South Sudan to extend their full cooperation to UNISFA and the JBVMM. This includes guaranteeing full and unrestricted freedom of movement, facilitating the reopening of team sites, including in Gok Machar, and expediting the issuance of outstanding visas for United Nations police and corrections personnel, whose presence is vital for maintaining the rule of law and protecting civilians.

Finally, we commend the courage and dedication of UNISFA’s peacekeepers and humanitarian personnel working under extremely challenging circumstances. The United Kingdom remains committed to supporting UNISFA and working with the parties and regional partners to achieve lasting peace and stability for the people of Abyei.
after.United States of America:
As penholder, the United States thanks Council members for their support and constructive engagement on the resolution just adopted, which renews the mandate of the United Nations Interim Security Force for Abyei (UNISFA) and its support for the Joint Border Verification and Monitoring Mechanism (JBVMM).

UNISFA plays an indispensable role in maintaining stability, protecting civilians, and facilitating local dialogue in Abyei. This mission is all the more vital today as the devastating conflict in Sudan continues to reverberate across borders, driving displacement, straining local resources, and hindering political dialogue between Sudan and South Sudan.

The resolution adopted today reaffirms the Council’s unwavering commitment to the stability of the Abyei Area and the peace of its communities. It sends a clear message that Abyei must remain demilitarized and weapons-free. We reiterate our call for the South Sudan People’s Defence Forces and any other armed elements to fully withdraw from the Abyei Area.

We also urge both Sudan and South Sudan to extend their full cooperation to UNISFA and the JBVMM. This includes guaranteeing full freedom of movement for peacekeepers, expediting the issuance of visas for United Nations police and personnel, operationalizing joint administrative and security institutions, and making tangible progress toward a peaceful political resolution on the final status of Abyei.

The United States commends the brave peacekeepers and personnel of UNISFA, as well as troop- and police-contributing countries, who carry out their critical duties under increasingly challenging conditions. We remain steadfast in our support for UNISFA, the people of Abyei, and efforts to achieve lasting peace and security in the region.

Thank you, Mr. President.
